source.title: SoftSAE: Dynamic Top-K Selection for Adaptive Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Jakub Stepien; M. Mazur; J. Tabor; P. Spurek

page_placements.theme: Sparsity, width and extraction choices determine feature granularity

record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse autoencoders to Gemma-2-2B activations and evaluates the resulting features; this is an LLM setting, not a reproduction of the toy-model superposition method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports feature-absorption and feature-splitting metrics for Gemma SAE architectures. Those metrics bear indirectly on V4. Reconstruction, sparsity-control, and CLIP results do not directly test the listed claim versions. The SCR and TPP table layout does not provide an unambiguous assignment of all values to metrics, so those values are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: A method paper: it proposes SoftSAE and benchmarks it against TopK, BatchTopK and Matryoshka SAEs on CLIP and Gemma-2-2B layer 12. Absorption and splitting compare SAE architectures with one another. They do not test whether the model's representations are superposed, spread across neurons, or contain sparse features an SAE recovers (V4). They also do not test SAE feature completeness, stability or canonicality (V5). The paper assumes superposition and SAE validity as background.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SoftSAE learns input-adaptive sparsity that tracks visual and textual complexity. They say it stays competitive on the reconstruction–sparsity trade-off and yields well-structured, disentangled features, particularly at higher sparsity levels. They list computational cost as the main limitation. They make no claim about superposition itself.
record.recipe_differences: Trains an adaptive sparse autoencoder using a Dynamic Sparsity MLP and differentiable Soft Top-K, then evaluates SAE feature quality; it does not reproduce Toy Models of Superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature absorption and splitting results vary with target sparsity and SAE architecture. The authors also state that masking method affects the predicted sparsity score, and that annealing yields modest, consistent improvements.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gemma-2-2B layer 12, SAE absorption fraction varies strongly by architecture at fixed k. At k=40, Matryoshka scores 0.056 while TopK scores 0.275. Splitting likewise varies with architecture and k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature-quality diagnostics (absorption, splitting) depend on SAE architecture and target sparsity. This is a method-comparison result, not a test of whether SAE features are canonical units.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the tabulated feature metrics. The claim-relevant LLM results concern one model and layer, and SAE feature metrics do not independently establish that native model features are sparse or distributed across neurons. The SCR/TPP table values are not unambiguously assignable from the provided flattened text.
record.rows_left_out: CLIP reconstruction/sparsity results and Gemma reconstruction/FVE results do not measure V4's feature-recovery claim. SCR and TPP values from Table 2 were left out because the provided table layout does not unambiguously map all values to the named metrics.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
No test of capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Does not measure feature spread across neurons. Does not test whether Gemma has sparse features an SAE recovers; SAE validity is assumed.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicality of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T3 to uses_without_test/T4. The paper treats superposition and SAE feature recovery as background, citing prior work in its introduction. All Gemma rows are SAE-architecture benchmark comparisons, so their versions are set to none. The SCR TOP 2 and TPP TOP 10 columns in Table 2 are in fact readable, contrary to the record, but they are also method comparisons and bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry are tested.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Does not measure feature distribution across neurons or independently establish that the model's native features are sparse; evaluates SAE-derived features on Gemma activations.
Does not test completeness, stability, or canonicality of SAE features.
Does not test whether model features are one-dimensional directions or multi-dimensional.
